[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC bob-cli-78[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Sub-project cascade for project blocking and the project pull-in[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]A blocked project's sub-projects (project notes whose `parent:` [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]names it, recursively) are Blocked too: their `^prj` and every open[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]resident are `[?]` and tagged `#prj_is_blocked`. `bob task [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]reconcile` derives this and reverses it when the ancestor's reasons[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]clear. The Task Card (Ctrl+Shift+P) applies and reverses it in the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]same gesture. Every other engine reads a tagged `^prj` as an [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]inherited reason, so nothing links, recovers, or pulls in a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]cascade-blocked task. Closing a sub-project's `^prj` that leaves [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]its parent with no open work pulls the parent's `^prj` in as Next [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim](§12.10 trigger (c)), both in bob capture and in Obsidian.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]8[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]4[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]
